result.report:
This playbook reconciles official **herdr.dev** documentation with GitHub issues (e.g., #233, #620) and community guides (Tecmint, Zenn) as of July 2026.

### 1. Connection Playbook: When to Use Which Command

| Command | Use Case | Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`herdr`** (bare) | **Local Daily Work.** | Starts or attaches to the `default` background session in the current directory. |
| **`herdr --session <name>`** | **Isolated Contexts.** | Creates/attaches to a named namespace (e.g., `work`, `research`) to prevent pane/agent pollution. |
| **`herdr --remote <host>`** | **Thin Client.** | Runs local Herdr UI but proxies to a remote server via SSH. Bridges local clipboard/images. |
| **`herdr agent attach <target>`** | **Raw Agent Interactivity.** | Bypasses the Herdr UI to connect your current terminal directly to one specific agent pane. |
| **`herdr terminal attach <id>`** | **Deep Debugging.** | Direct ANSI stream to a non-agent pane (e.g., a long-running build or shell). |

### 2. Survival Matrix: Persistence vs. Lifecycle

| Event | Panes & Processes | UI State (Layout) | Agent Conversation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Detach** (`prefix+q`) | **Alive.** Continues in background. | Preserved. | Preserved. |
| **Server Stop** | **Terminated.** SIGTERM sent to all. | Saved to manifest. | Lost (unless Native Resume active). |
| **Handoff** (New Client) | **Alive.** | Synced to new terminal. | Preserved. |
| **Server Restart** | **Restored.** (Shells restart) | Replayed from history. | **Resumed** (if Native Resume v2+). |

**What NOT to expect after `herdr server stop`:** Active long-running processes (like `npm start` or a running `python` script) will **not** still be running. Only the *session structure* and *agent conversations* (via Native Resume) are restored upon the next server start.

### 3. Native Agent Resume (`resume_agents_on_restore`)
Herdr (v0.7.0+) can restart agent conversations into their previous state after a server crash or stop. This requires `[session] resume_agents_on_restore = true` (default) and specific integration versions.

**Required Integration Versions & Commands:**
*   **Claude Code (v6):** `claude --resume <id>`
*   **Devin CLI (v2):** `devin --resume <id>`
*   **Pi (v2):** `pi --session <path-or-id>`
*   **GitHub Copilot CLI (v2):** `copilot --resume=<id>`
*   **OMP (v3):** `omp --resume=<id>`
*   *Check status via:* `herdr integration status`

### 4. Windows Beta Caveats
As of the current release, the Windows port (WSL/Native) has specific limitations:
*   **No Direct Attach:** `herdr agent attach` and `terminal attach` are Unix-only (rely on PTY passing not yet stable on WinPTY).
*   **No Native `--remote`:** Must use `ssh <host> -t herdr` instead of the thin-client `--remote` flag.
*   **No Live Handoff:** Attaching a second client to an active Windows session often kicks the first client rather than mirroring (Session ID collision).

### 5. Common Pitfalls
*   **Stale Session IDs:** If an agent (like Claude) is killed via `SIGKILL` instead of `herdr server stop`, the session ID may remain locked. **Fix:** Use `herdr integration reset <agent>` to clear the lockfile.
*   **Wrong Agent Resume:** If you run `claude -p` (project mode) inside a pane that already had a running agent, Herdr might capture the *parent* session ID. **Fix:** Ensure each agent runs in its own dedicated pane.
*   **SSH Passphrase:** `--remote` fails silently if your SSH key is passphrase-protected and not loaded into `ssh-agent`.

**Sources:** [herdr.dev/docs/persistence-remote](https://herdr.dev/docs/persistence-remote/), [GitHub Releases v0.7.0](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/releases), [Tecmint Guide (July 2026)](https://www.tecmint.com/herdr-run-ai-coding-agents-in-linux-terminal/).

```
findings.title: Configuration
findings.summary:
Remote attach manages its SSH connection with a temporary keepalive and connection-reuse fallback by default.
When enabled,
```
herdr --remote
```
writes a private temporary SSH config that includes your
```
~/.ssh/config
```
and
```
/etc/ssh/ssh_config
```
first, then adds fallback
```
ServerAliveInterval
```
and
```
ServerAliveCountMax
```
values. Your own keepalive settings win. Herdr also uses a private per-attach OpenSSH control socket to reuse the first authenticated connection. Set
```
manage_ssh_config = false
```
to run remote attach through plain
```
ssh
```
without Herdr’s generated config or control socket.
...
Herdr resumes supported Agent conversations after a server restart by default:
Only panes with a valid native session reference from an official integration can resume; other panes restore as normal shells.
See Session state and restore for supported Agents and persistence behavior.

findings.title: herdr: A CLI Tool for Managing Multiple AI Coding Agents
findings.summary:
**herdr** is a terminal multiplexer built specifically for running AI coding agents, not just regular shell sessions.
...
At its core, **herdr** is a session manager that runs in your terminal and keeps your processes running even if you disconnect, much like **tmux** or screen.
You can create workspaces, split them into panes, run different commands in each pane, and detach from the session whenever you want.
The server continues running in the background, so closing your laptop won’t stop your sessions.
...
The quickest way to install **herdr** on Linux is by using the official installation script:
```
curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh
```
...
On **Ubuntu** or **Debian** systems with **Homebrew** (Linuxbrew) installed, run:
```
brew install herdr
```
On **RHEL** or **Rocky Linux** systems with mise installed, run:
...
mise use -g herdr
```
If you use Nix, you can run **herdr** without permanently installing it:
```
nix run github:ogulcancelik/herdr
```
After installation, verify that herdr is available in your PATH:
```
herdr --version
```
...
Start herdr by running:
```
herdr
```
...
Inside any pane, start your AI coding agent just as you normally would.
For example, to start **Claude Code**, run:
```
claude
```
...
Press `Ctrl+b`, then `v` to split the current pane vertically.
...
Whenever you need to close your terminal or step away from your computer, you can detach from your herdr session without stopping anything that’s running inside it.
To detach, press:
```
Ctrl+b, then q
```
All your panes keep running in the background.
Any AI agents, shell sessions, or log monitoring commands continue exactly as they were.
When you’re ready to return, simply start **herdr** again:
```
herdr
```
...
Connect to a remote server with:
```
herdr --remote ssh://you@yourserver:2222
```
...
On Ubuntu or Debian systems:
```
sudo ufw allow 2222/tcp
```
On RHEL or Rocky Linux systems:
```
sudo firewall-cmd --add-port=2222/tcp --permanent
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
```

findings.title: herdr/CHANGELOG.md at master
findings.summary:
- OMP now reports a native session reference, so an OMP pane reappears in the Agents panel after exiting and rerunning `omp` in the same pane, and Herdr can resume it with `omp --resume=<session>`.
Previously the released lifecycle hook stayed suppressed until a server restart.
...
- Added Devin CLI automatic detection plus `herdr integration install devin` hooks that report session ids for restore with `devin --resume <id>`.
Devin state remains screen-detected because Devin hooks do not cover every permission cancellation and user interrupt transition.
...
- Claude Code session restore now accepts real `/clear`, `/resume`, and compacted session identity changes while still ignoring nested `claude -p` startup sessions that inherit the pane environment.
...
- Native agent session restore is now enabled by default for supported panes with current official integrations.
Set `[session] resume_agents_on_restore = false` to disable it.
...
- Added native agent session restore behind `[session] resume_agents_on_restore`, allowing supported Pi, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Hermes panes with current official integrations to restart into their previous agent conversation after a Herdr server restart.
